_meta.scope: Complete key-action vocabulary the vendor stack (NayaFlow 1.25.1: Electron main + flow-bg-server.exe + NayaCore.exe) can name and can flash to the Naya Create keyboard.
_meta.correction_to_task_premise: NayaFlow's Electron main bundle (asar/dist/main/index.js) contains NO action model, no SQL and no ZMQ protocol: byte-level grep for MODULE_FORCE_CHARGING, LED_BRIGHTNESS_UP, actionType, key_bindings, CREATE TABLE returns 0 hits. Its only relevant code (byte offsets ~1419800-1425600) spawns installed-tree/flow/flow-bg-server.exe (a Go/gin binary, 25.7 MB) with env NAYA_CORE_EXE_DIR and pipes JSON-RPC. The SQLite schema, migrations (goose), the embedded action catalog (data.ActionsJSON, 652 records) and the template seeds live in flow-bg-server.exe; its strings dump is extracted/NayaFlow-1.25.1/strings/flow-strings.txt (6.5 MB; the file starts with the PE header and a 'Go build ID'). The renderer bundle asar/dist/renderer/assets/index-mihUmo_8.js holds the UI-side action typing ($s class) and the feature flags.

hid_keyboard_names_note: 248 names, HID page 0x07, in NayaCore.exe order (A-Z from 0x77afb4, then 0x77b018-0x77b9d8). ZMK-style aliases that resolve to the same usage: HASH/POUND, DELETE/DEL, INTERNATIONAL_n/INTn, LANGUAGE_n/LANGn/LANG_HANGEUL/LANG_HANJA/LANG_KATAKANA/LANG_HIRAGANA/LANG_ZENKAKUHANKAKU/LANG_ZENKAKUHANKAKU2/LANG_HANJA2/LANG_HANJA3, SYSREQ/ATTENTION. Shifted symbols (EXCLAMATION, AT_SIGN, HASH, DOLLAR, PERCENT, CARET, AMPERSAND, ASTERISK, LEFT/RIGHT_PARENTHESIS, UNDERSCORE, PLUS, LEFT/RIGHT_BRACE, PIPE, TILDE2, COLON, DOUBLE_QUOTES, TILDE, LESS_THAN, GREATER_THAN, QUESTION, CLEAR2, PIPE2) are encoded as base usage + modifier byte 0x02 (LSHIFT). K_PLAY_PAUSE..K_CALCULATOR are the keyboard-page (0x07) media usages 0xE8-0xFB; K_LOCK, K_SCREENSAVER and K_COFFEE all encode usage 0xF9 exactly as in ZMK keys.h. No name in NayaCore carries a _JIS, _MAC or other locale suffix.
hid_system_names_note: HID page 0x01 usages 0x81/0x82/0x83 (param entries 0-2). Present in NayaCore only; not in the bg-server catalog.
consumer_names_note: 27 names, HID page 0x0C (param entries 222-248: 0x30,0x31,0x32,0x34,0x40-0x48,0x60,0x61,0x6F,0x70,0xB3-0xB8,0xCD,0xE2,0xE9,0xEA). The bg-server catalog exposes only C_POWER, C_BRIGHTNESS_DEC, C_BRIGHTNESS_INC, C_MUTE, C_VOL_DOWN, C_VOL_UP, C_PLAY_PAUSE, C_PREVIOUS, C_NEXT, C_REWIND, C_FAST_FORWARD (11).

modifier_alias_table.note: This run sits between the LED names and the naya-integration names and is the token set NayaCore accepts as modifiers when it splits composite codes on ' + '. LCTRL/LSHIFT/LALT/LGUI/RCTRL/RSHIFT/RALT/RGUI are almost certainly members too but their literals are pooled with the HID-key run and cannot be attributed. RIGHT_ALT, RIGHT_GUI, RIGHT_META, RIGHT_WIN, RIGHT_COMMAND, RMETA, RCMD, RWIN do not exist anywhere in NayaCore.exe. The renderer's own modifier list is [LGUI,RGUI,LCTRL,RCTRL,LALT,RALT,LSHFT,RSHFT,LSHIFT,RSHIFT]; LSHFT/RSHFT are NOT NayaCore names.

led_params_note: Decoded from the 19 (argument, subcommand) pairs at 0x77adc8. Memory order is EFFECT_ON_OFF, BRIGHTNESS_UP, BRIGHTNESS_DOWN, SPEED_UP, SPEED_DOWN, EFFECT, the nine colours, then BREATHE, SOLID, SWIRL, SPEC -- i.e. not the string order; names were assigned by matching the known subcommand semantics (0x00 toggle, 0x07/0x08 brightness, 0x09/0x0a speed, 0x0b cycle, 0x0d select effect 0 solid/1 breathe/2 swirl/3 spectrum, 0x0f colour). Colour argument is ZMK's RGB_COLOR_HSB packing (h<<16 | s<<8 | b): red h0, green 120, blue 240, white s0, cyan 180, magenta 270, yellow 60, orange 30, pink 300, all b=100. All 19 are exposed in the bg-server catalog (frontendType LED, tab Extended, group Lighting) and seeded into templates.
bluetooth_params_note: (argument, command) pairs at 0x77af20; command numbering is ZMK's bt behaviour (0 clear, 1 next, 2 prev, 3 select). Name assignment for BT_CLEAR=(0,0) matches the known '(0,0) clear' wire fact; BT_NEXT/BT_PREV/BT_SELECT_SL by ZMK command order; BT_DEVICE_n=(n,3) matches the known '(3,n)'. Catalog exposes only BT_DEVICE_1..4 and BT_CLEAR (frontendType bluetooth, group Connection); BT_NEXT, BT_PREV, BT_SELECT_SL are NayaCore-only.

mouse_params.note: M1..M5 = (button mask, command 3) pairs at 0x77aef0, matching the known 'mouse on a key = (3, mask)' wire fact (memory stores argument first). Catalog aliases MOUSE_1..MOUSE_5 (+_JIS) map to actionCode M1..M5.
mouse_params.module_only_note: These have display formats 'MOUSE_STATIC<%1<%2)', 'STATIC_SCROLL_Y<%1)', 'STATIC_SCROLL_X<%1)', 'STATIC_ZOOM<%1)' in Naya_Binding.cpp and are the Track/Touch gesture slot values; none is in the catalog by that name (the catalog's module 'value' codes are 'mouse - MOUSE_LEFT - MOUSE_RIGHT', 'mouse - MOUSE_DOWN - MOUSE_UP', 'mouse - SCROLL_UP - SCROLL_DOWN', 'mouse - SCROLL_LEFT - SCROLL_RIGHT').

layer_behaviours_note: $ID is replaced by the layer UUID (seeds: 'MO_LAYER_<uuid>' with actionType layer_polite_hold, 15 rows). NayaCore has no 'MO_LAYER'/'_LAYER_' literal; it dispatches on the action_type word and resolves the layer from the code's last '_' token (cf. 'Layer (%1) not found for layer navigation action in module config id:%2'). All four have serializer length checks and are flashable; only layer_polite_hold appears in shipped templates.

other_behaviours.sticky_key: Record type 0x0a exists only as the word 'sticky_key' in the record-type table (0x3ee298). No param-length check in Binding::readBytes (the checked set is KEY_PRESS, TO_LAYER, TOGGLE_LAYER, MO, STICKY_LAYER, BLUETOOTH, RGB_UG, OUTPUTS, NAYA_INTEGRATIONS, MOUSE), no action name, no app action_type, no catalog record, no display format. Named, not flashable.
other_behaviours.grave_escape: Record type 0x04, same situation as sticky_key: only the word 'grave_escape' at 0x3ee250. Named, not flashable.
other_behaviours.macro: Record type 0x02: the word 'macro' at 0x3ee23c; CDC command names [READ/WRITE MACRO LIST/DATA 0x exist (core-strings.txt 5735-5738) but there is no _remapRead/WriteMacro* process step, no _interpretMacro*, no SQL query against macros/*_macro_steps in Naya_SQLReader, no 'MACRO' action name, no length check; 'Maximum macros exceeded.' (1699) is an error enum string. The bg-server has full macro CRUD (macros + loop/text/mouse/standard/wait_for_release _action_macro_steps) and the renderer resolves macro bindings (actionType 'macro', code '<...>_<macroId>'), but the renderer ships macros:{enabled:!1} and Dn('macros') hides the 'Macros & Shortcuts' onboarding item; no seed row uses actionType macro. Named on the app side, not flashable by NayaCore (consistent with the measured 2026-09-07 result: NayaCore writes NONE).
other_behaviours.mod_tap: Record type 0x03. NayaCore serializes it as a per-key tap/hold PAIR: naya_remap::Key::serializeBindingPairData, 'Cannot serialize mod-tap pair with missing binding (tap: %1, hold: %2)', 'Bytes with MOD_TAP identifier are too small, expected at least 21 bytes' (Naya_Key.cpp), plus the key_bindings.behavior words tap/hold/double_tap/tap_hold at 0x3f0904 and settings 'tapping term ms' / 'tap hold flavour'. So it is flashable, but only via two key_bindings rows (behavior 'tap' + 'hold') on one key -- there is no standalone MOD_TAP action code or catalog record. The renderer knows the behaviour list ['tap','tap_hold','double_tap','hold','press'] but the flags advancedBehaviors and behaviorToggle are false (and never even read); every shipped seed row uses behavior 'press'. 'core' and 'core_toggle_hold_morph' at 0x3f0878/0x3f0880 are NayaCore app-action-types with no catalog user and may be the hold-morph path.

uncertain: Everything here is string/data-table evidence; no disassembly was done (no capstone/objdump available). 'Flashable' means a serializer artefact exists in NayaCore, not that firmware honours the record.

The naya-integration ids 150/151/200/201/300/301/400 are matched to TUNE_MODE_L/R, WINDOWS_OS/MAC_OS, SCROLL_DIRECTION_L/R, MODULE_CHARGING purely by table position; only 401 = MODULE_FORCE_CHARGING is independently known.

The key_param_table name column is inferred from HID usage semantics (ZMK keys.h order), because two spots (KP_CLEAR 0xD8 at entry 191; consumer tail entries 239-248 ordered by usage number) show the string run and the param table are not emitted in the same order.

All in-memory pairs (rgb_ug, bluetooth, mouse) are stored (argument, subcommand); the known wire order is (subcommand, argument). Either NayaCore swaps on emit or the wire notes are transposed -- not resolvable from strings.
BT_SELECT_SL=(0,3) would select profile 0 while BT_DEVICE_1=(1,3) selects 1; whether the firmware is 0- or 1-based is unknown.
NayaCore's dispatch word is 'Value' (capital V, 0x3f0898) while the bg-server writes action_type 'value'; a case-insensitive compare is assumed since 54 seeded module rows use it.
NayaCore has no 'press' literal although every seeded key row has behavior 'press'; presumably any behavior word other than tap/hold/double_tap/tap_hold is treated as the plain slot.
NayaCore app action types 'core', 'core_toggle_hold_morph', 'configuration_rude_toggle', 'configuration_rude_toggle_l', 'configuration_rude_toggle_r' have no catalog record and unknown semantics.
